description: Our goal is to develop a health monitoring software that tracks astronauts' physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions. We aim to identify potential health risks caused by microgravity, radiation, and isolation, helping astronauts maintain their health and making future space exploration safer.
summary: We, as a team, developed a software that analyzes and monitors astronouts both physical and mental health through their daily patterns, stress levels, sleep schedules and working demands.
details: GRACE (Guided Resilience & Astronaut Care Environment) is an autonomous, offline-first crew health support system engineered for long-duration deep-space transit missions to overcome communication latencies of up to twenty minutes. Operating locally through an encrypted SQLite and AES-256 vault, the platform continuously correlates physiological telemetry streams—such as resting heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, and ARED resistance exercise metrics—with voluntary behavioral self-assessments regarding sleep duration and perceived cognitive stress. Rather than functioning as a diagnostic medical device, GRACE utilizes an explainable decision-support engine to evaluate incoming data against individual pre-flight baselines, alerting astronauts to sustained cross-domain fatigue driftand generating actionable, localized countermeasure checklists like circadian lighting shifts and workload deferrals. Aligned with NASA Human Research Program behavioral health goals, NASA-STD-3001 crew health standards, and Deep Space Network (DSN) constraints, GRACE preserves crew data ownership and mission performance during interplanetary isolation.
